entities.summary:
The Nian Rebellion was a complex series of civil wars and internal conflicts that took place in China from the 1850s to the 1860s. This period of chaos was sparked by the Taiping Rebellion, a millenarian Christian Movement that rose up against the Qing dynasty. The Nian Rebellion played a crucial role in the eventual downfall of the Qing dynasty and the rise of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.

The Nian Rebellion was characterized by its brutal violence, with estimates suggesting that between 20 and 30 million people lost their lives during the conflict. The rebellion was marked by a series of brutal massacres, including the killing of the entire population of the city of Xiang. The conflict also saw the rise of powerful warlords who would go on to play a significant role in the subsequent Qing dynasty.

The Nian Rebellion had a profound impact on the course of Chinese history, paving the way for the eventual fall of the Qing dynasty in 1912. The rebellion also saw the rise of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, which would go on to play a significant role in the subsequent history of China. The Nian Rebellion's legacy can be seen in the continued tensions between the Han Chinese and the ethnic minorities of China.

As the famous Chinese historian, Chen Xianping, noted, 'The Nian Rebellion was a crucial turning point in Chinese history, marking the end of the Qing dynasty and the beginning of a new era in Chinese politics.'
